concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: Before the amendment takes effect on 1 October 2026, the DPA requires the Processor to notify the Controller no later than 48 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach. The amendment signed on 15 September 2026 does not alter this until its effective date.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amended breach notification clause requires notice no later than 24 hours after awareness of a Personal Data Breach, and this amendment is effective from 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment reduces the on-site audit notice period from 30 days to 20 days, effective from 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amended liability clause sets the Processor's aggregate liability for DPA breaches at a fixed EUR 1,000,000, which applies regardless of the fees paid, from 1 October 2026.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The amended liability clause expressly states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap does not apply to breaches of the Confidentiality section.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd is listed as an approved Sub-processor at the DPA's Effective Date, and its withdrawal only takes effect on 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: The approval of Meridian Mail Ltd is withdrawn with effect from 1 January 2027, so it is no longer an approved Sub-processor by 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, personal data is processed or stored in Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, France and Denmark. Ireland drops out because Meridian Mail's approval was withdrawn on 1 January 2027, while France and Denmark were added on that date.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: Under the amended 60-day deletion period, counted from the 31 December 2026 termination date (excluding the trigger date and including the final date), the deadline falls on 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa. the notice must describe the breach's nature, affected data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting data processed under the DPA. The notice must describe the breach's nature, affected data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed.
justifications: The amended breach clause sets the 24-hour outer limit, and the content requirements for notices remain unchanged from the original DPA.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: Usable privileged credentials were confirmed exposed on 10 April 2027 at 04:30, which triggers the expedited 12-hour outer limit rather than the standard 24-hour limit. The expedited limit applies even though the credential exposure was confirmed after original awareness.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness occurred at 17:10 on 9 April 2027, so the 12-hour expedited outer limit expired at 05:10 on 10 April. The first notice was delivered at 06:00, which is 50 minutes later.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: Counting from awareness on Friday 9 April, the 12 April closure is skipped and 14 April is excluded as the only approved pause day, so the third Business Day is 16 April. The refused 16 April pause request has no effect.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The ordinary 60-day deletion period from the 30 June 2027 termination ends 29 August 2027, and held records must be deleted by the later of that date and the tenth Business Day after the last hold ends (25 August 2027). Business Days are taken as Monday to Friday.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: Backup BK-0630 was created on 30 June 2027 and contains no held records, so it must be deleted within 35 calendar days of creation, which is earlier than its ordinary deadline. Restoration does not restart this period.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: After termination, records retained under a legal hold may be used only for legal preservation, with service delivery and analytics excluded. The Controller also rejected the request to keep the records for analytics.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval begins no earlier than the latest of the proposed start date, the written Controller consent, and the completed security review, which was 22 April for the Stockholm service in Sweden. Actual processing in Stockholm also began on that date.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS was added as an approved Sub-processor for transactional email delivery from 1 January 2027 and continues ordinary transactional email from France. Meridian Mail Ltd's approval was withdrawn, and its later emergency permission is limited to one incident and does not cover ordinary customer email.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: Personal Data is stored in Norway and Estonia, and Cendrillon Mail SAS processes email from France under effective approval. Sweden has actual processing in Stockholm from 22 April 2027 under the consent and completed security review for that service. Denmark, Ireland, Finland, Germany, and Lithuania do not meet both conditions on 15 May 2027.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: The security cap is the greater of EUR 2,000,000 and twice Qualifying Fees, which are EUR 1,140,000 after removing VAT and the same-period service credit. Twice that amount is EUR 2,280,000, which exceeds EUR 2,000,000.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year, and EUR 300,000 in ordinary payments has already been made in that year. The remaining ordinary pool is therefore EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: The remaining ordinary pool of EUR 700,000 caps L-1, and the remaining security pool of EUR 1,780,000 covers the EUR 1,750,000 security loss L-2 in full. Confidentiality losses L-3 and L-4 are uncapped and total EUR 350,000, giving EUR 2,800,000 in total.
